sources.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos lecture notes (2026 author-hosted revision, 236 pp.)
sources.locator: §4.3.1 printed pp. 84-87 and §5.1-§5.6 printed pp. 95-133 (PDF pp. 103-141) of the 236-page author-hosted 2026 revision: §5.1-§5.1.4 four-vectors, proper time, indices and tensors pp. 95-102; §5.2-§5.2.1 conserved currents pp. 102-105; §5.3-§5.3.5 gauge potentials, the electromagnetic tensor, its transformation law and the two Lorentz scalars pp. 105-113; §5.4-§5.4.2 the covariant Maxwell equations, the Lorentz force law and motion in constant fields pp. 113-118; §5.5 the action pp. 118-127; §5.6-§5.6.3 energy and momentum conservation, the energy-momentum tensor and angular momentum pp. 127-133. Read from the full extracted text of the revision retained in reader-tong; the source's (+---) metric, A_mu=(phi/c,-A) potential and overall F sign are converted to the framework's (-+++), F_0i=-E_i/c dictionary in every use below.

contents.name: §5.1-§5.1.4 pp. 95-102: four-vectors, proper time, raising and lowering indices, and the general tensor transformation law (5.3)-(5.10)
contents.support: The index conventions (eta raising and lowering, contravariant/covariant component laws, constant Lambda) are absorbed into the component computations of the equivalence and covariance proofs; the framework's own conventions are fixed by [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and the in-run supplier [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]].

contents.name: §5.2-§5.2.1 pp. 102-105: conserved currents, the four-current and its transformation, and magnetism as a relativistic effect of moving charges
contents.reason: The four-current, frame density and continuity are fixed by the framework's def-em-sources and the charge-continuity items on the earlier primitives page; this page consumes only the tensor-component identification and does not re-derive current conservation.

contents.name: §5.3-§5.3.2 pp. 105-108: gauge invariance, the electromagnetic tensor (5.15) and its transformation law (5.16)
contents.support: The source displays the antisymmetric field tensor and the component law F' = Lambda F Lambda^T that the scaffold's covariance clause (b) uses after sign conversion to the framework's dictionary.

contents.name: §5.3.3 p. 109: boosted infinite line charge worked example
contents.reason: The noncompact infinite-line source application is outside the current retarded-source branches. pthm-em-retarded-potentials requires smooth compact spacetime support; pthm-em-lienard-wiechert handles one prescribed proper point trajectory. Neither interface supplies the boosted infinite-line source. The general field boost remains fully supplied by the covariance pair.

contents.name: §5.3.4 pp. 110-111: boosted point charge worked example
contents.reason: A prescribed uniformly subluminal constant-velocity C3 point trajectory is a specialization of pthm-em-lienard-wiechert and its point-history potential supplier, off the worldline. The compact smooth source theorem is not used for this eternal nonzero point charge. The covariance pair retains its own constant-field boost example; no source-specific infinite-line result is attributed to the point branch.

contents.name: §5.3.5 pp. 111-113: the two Lorentz scalars (5.23) and (5.25), with the alternating tensor and the dual field
contents.support: The two invariant combinations B^2-E^2/c^2 and E.B and the dual tensor are exactly the invariant clause (b) of the boost/covariance theorem; the source's dual and overall sign are converted to the framework's dictionary.

contents.name: §5.4 pp. 113-115: the Maxwell equations in tensor form, the sourced equation and the dual homogeneous equation
contents.support: The source's covariant Maxwell system is the physical content shown equivalent to the four laboratory equations in clause (a), after the framework's sign and index conventions are imposed.

contents.name: §5.4.1 pp. 115-116: the Lorentz force law (5.30) and its unpacking to dp/dt = q(E+u x B) (5.32) and d(energy)/dt = qE.u (5.33)
contents.support: The source derivation of the coordinate force and power from m dU/dtau = qF^{mu nu}U_nu is the scaffold's clause (a), with the framework's four-velocity and index conventions.

contents.name: §5.4.2 pp. 116-118: motion in constant fields, the relativistic trajectory in a uniform electric field and its limiting speed
contents.support: The source's uniform-electric-field trajectory is reproduced by the scaffold's exact solution r(t) = r_0 + (c/h)(sqrt(1+h^2t^2)-1)e_1 with the subluminal bound, after SI conversion.

contents.name: §5.5-§5.5.3 pp. 118-127: the particle and Maxwell actions, stationarity and the theta term
contents.reason: The action formulation, its stationary-action model and the gauge/source compatibility are the subject of the later action pair (order 357), which requires this covariance page; no action content is scaffolded here.

contents.name: §5.6.1 pp. 127-130: local energy and momentum conservation and the identification of the two conserved four-vectors
contents.support: The source's continuity equations for energy and momentum are the vector identities that the tensor balance clause (c) of the scaffold refines; the framework's vector identities were independently scaffolded on the earlier balance page.

contents.name: §5.6.2 pp. 130-132: the energy-momentum tensor (5.49), its transformation law (5.50), the divergence identity and tracelessness
contents.support: The source constructs the quadratic tensor from F, proves symmetry and tracelessness and computes the divergence against the four-force density, exactly the route of the scaffold's clauses (a)-(c) in the framework's sign conventions.

contents.name: §5.6.3 pp. 132-133: angular momentum conservation and the symmetry requirement on the stress tensor
contents.support: The divergence-free angular current x^mu T^{lambda nu} - x^nu T^{lambda mu} of clause (d) is the covariant form of the source's continuity equation for L = x x P, whose derivation uses the same symmetry of the stress block.

contents.name: §4.3.1 pp. 84-87: the monochromatic plane wave with positive angular frequency, the dispersion relation omega^2 = c^2 k^2 and the right-moving profile (4.15)-(4.16)
contents.support: The source's plane-wave data (positive omega, wavevector, dispersion relation) are the input to the scaffold's null-covector and frequency-reading clause; the item itself consumes the framework's def-em-plane-wave-definition and pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell scaffolded on the earlier waves page.

contents.name: node 127: the force on a moving charge (f = e(E + u x B) and F_{mu nu}U^mu U^nu = 0)

contents.name: node 128: the electromagnetic energy tensor and its balance identities

contents.name: §9.1 pp. 9.1-9.5: Poincaré transformations
contents.reason: Poincaré and Lorentz transformation kinematics are the subject of the run's earlier special-relativity pages; this covariance pair consumes them only through declared SR suppliers.

contents.name: §9.2 pp. 9.5-9.8: tensors and their transformation behaviour
contents.support: The covariance of component equations under constant Lorentz matrices is absorbed into the proof of the equivalence's covariance clause; the framework's conventions come from the in-run SR tensor supplier.

contents.name: §9.3 pp. 9.8-9.10: the field-strength tensor, four-current, inhomogeneous and homogeneous Maxwell equations and the dual
contents.support: The source's covariant Maxwell system (9.42)-(9.48) is the content shown equivalent to the laboratory equations; the source's sign of F is converted so that F_0i=-E_i/c and the sourced equation reads partial_mu F^{mu nu} = -mu_0 j^nu.

contents.name: §9.4 pp. 9.12-9.13: charged particles, proper-time parametrisation, four-momentum and the covariant Lorentz force (9.67)-(9.71)
